signals_note: An HTML page: recognised by its address and the heading that opens the board section, never by a name or a phrase in a person's bio. A page none of the shapes recognises is a drop-note, counted, with its reason.

board role: role basis: stated beside the name, or the heading's

notes: The declared tier (ruling 72): the board the party itself declares on its own website, as the Internet Archive or the old job captured the page. Only the board's own section is read: a members' council, a wise council, staff ('management / board support'), MPs and candidates on the same page are not the board. A page is a claim by the party on the day captured; it can be stale. Contact lines and promoter statements (which can print a home address) are never read into a row. A deterministic read: no model.
applies_to: var/staging/party-boards/archive/** in the live old folder, captured 2017 onward (ruling 71)

h2
shapes.drop: a board heading over columns that do not pair: a role heading ('Co-leaders') over two names in two columns, and a role above its name in a third; which name holds which role is not in the markup

refuse.reason: a theme's placeholder people ('John Doe'), not the party's

process: Decode the bytes (gzip, zstandard), cut the Archive's toolbar, take the page as lines with their markup.
Refuse a page a refusal marker matches (a theme's placeholder people).
Take the first shape whose address rule and opening heading match; read its section in its form.
Every name is checked by the name rule; what fails is set aside with its reason.
gates: Every page in the window is a reading or a drop-note.
Every name read is a row or a catch-log line.
on_fail: drop-note the page or set aside the line; publish the rest
